# StreamingService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("StreamingService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Controls world streaming. A world too large to keep loaded is divided into a grid of cells, and this service loads and unloads cells by their distance from the focuses a game sets, usually the character or the camera. The work done each frame is limited by time, not by a number of cells.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the world streams. Turning it off freezes the current state: nothing new is loaded and nothing loaded is unloaded. Use it to hold the world still during an operation. |
| `LoadRadius` | `number` | `1024` | read/write | The distance from a focus within which the engine tries to keep cells loaded, in meters. A cell inside it is loaded when time allows. A loaded cell is unloaded only beyond a somewhat larger distance, so a focus at a boundary does not load and unload the same cell repeatedly. |
| `MinRadius` | `number` | `512` | read/write | The distance from a focus within which cells must be loaded, in meters. Everything inside it is loaded before a focus moves into it, so a character never walks into an area that has not loaded. See `PauseOutsideLoadedArea` for what happens when the area is not ready. |
| `PauseOutsideLoadedArea` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the simulation waits while the area within `MinRadius` is not loaded. With it off, a character can fall through ground that has not loaded. While waiting, ticks do not advance; nothing is rolled back.<br><br>It has no effect on a client, which cannot pause a simulation it does not control. A client holds its camera and shows that it is loading instead. |
| `StructureLoadRadius` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The distance from a focus within which cells of structures are kept loaded, in meters. It works like `LoadRadius`. At 0, `LoadRadius` is used. |
| `StructureMinRadius` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The distance within which cells of structures must be loaded, in meters. It lets large structures use a larger radius than small detail. At 0, the default, `MinRadius` is used. |
| `TerrainLoadRadius` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The distance from a focus within which cells of terrain features are kept loaded, in meters. At 0, `LoadRadius` is used. A saved `Terrain` and a block world that are streamed in cells are also kept to this radius.<br><br>A terrain cell holds a few large objects, so raising this radius costs much less than raising the radius for detail. |
| `TerrainMinRadius` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The distance within which cells of terrain features must be loaded, in meters. It is usually the largest of the three, so the horizon reaches farther than the objects on it. At 0, `MinRadius` is used.<br><br>It also applies to a saved `Terrain` and a block world that are streamed in cells. When a world first loads, the simulation waits until the ground within this radius has loaded, so nothing falls through it. |

## Methods

### `AddFocus(instance: Instance)`

Adds an instance as a focus, so that the world also streams around it. A focus is usually the character or the camera. There can be several, and a cell is kept loaded if any focus needs it. Raises an error for an instance that has no position in the world.

### `LoadAreaAsync(position: vector, radius: number)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Yields until everything within `radius` of `position` is loaded, both the cells of parts and the terrain. Call it before teleporting a character, so that the destination exists on arrival. Also call it at startup before `Terrain:HeightAt`, which returns nil for terrain that has not loaded.

It returns immediately if the area is already loaded. Raises an error if the world has no cells there.

### `RemoveFocus(instance: Instance)`

Removes an instance as a focus. Removing the last focus does not unload the world: what is loaded stays loaded.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `AreaLoaded(position: vector, radius: number)`

Fires when an area requested by a script has finished loading.

### `InstanceStreamedOut(instance: Instance)`

Fires for each instance that is streamed out while a script still holds a reference to it. Such an instance is not destroyed: its parent becomes nil, so the reference stays valid and the instance can still be read. An instance that no script refers to is destroyed, and this event does not fire for it.
